name: CA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting D+7 partisan lean makes the seat fundamentally Democratic
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at roughly 96%
McGuire has out-raised Gallagher and draws outside support
Political environment favors Democrats this cycle
model.rationale: The redrawn district carries a seven-point Democratic lean and the environment favors Democrats, while markets price a Democratic win near certain; Gallagher's incumbency and his cash-on-hand edge only modestly offset those advantages.
model.watch: Any general-election polling showing Gallagher running close, or a late shift in the national environment toward Republicans, would warrant revisiting this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's first district was redrawn to include more Democratic-leaning North Coast territory, leaving it with a seven-point Democratic partisan lean. State Senator Mike McGuire, the Democratic nominee, has out-raised incumbent Republican James Gallagher and benefits from outside spending on his behalf, though Gallagher holds a modest cash-on-hand advantage. No public polls of the general election are available, and no expert raters have weighed in on the race.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 96 percent, and the underlying fundamentals point the same direction: the district lean, a favorable environment, and McGuire's fundraising edge. Gallagher's incumbency provides some offset, but not enough to close a gap of this size. The race rates as Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the absence of direct polling in this newly configured district.
